correctness.rationale: Conditional on T=t>0, independent gamma-subordinator energy factors have gamma shape k=at and rate b; normalized Gaussian multipole sums have chi-square dimension d=2l+1. Kolmogorov strong laws yield means eta*k and eta^2*k(k+1), so both unknowns have almost-surely consistent rational inverse estimators. Chi-square perturbations have accumulated conditional mean/variance O(log L), negligible at sqrt(L), giving the explicit bivariate conditional gamma CLT and verified delta-method covariance. The global array is a parameter-free Gaussian kernel of W=theta*a*T/b and recovers W a.s.; strictly positive mixing densities imply mutual absolute continuity and a strict testing-error floor; gamma consistency implies pairwise singular laws. The energy-dispersion classifier has a conditional Markov bound O((log L)/L^(3/4)). The standalone checker was replayed from its actual path and passed 780 rational identities. No finite algebra check is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The two classes recently introduced as alternatives have equal second-order spectra yet exhibit sharply different infinite-data inferential laws (mutual singularity versus equivalence). The explicit jointly consistent amplitude/latent-clock estimators and their conditional covariance quantify what one complete sky can reveal; the global mixture reduction states an impossibility no additional harmonic resolution can overcome. The contrast is a motivated spectral-inference obstruction, not a standalone textbook gamma moment calculation.
